result: In 128 ME/CFS and chronic fatigue patients, IgA responses to LPS of 6 enterobacteria correlated positively with serum IL-1, TNFa, neopterin and elastase; patients with abnormally high IgA had higher cytokines, neopterin and IBS ratings, and IL-1, TNFa and neopterin were higher in ME/CFS than CF.
reason: Same anti-LPS IgA measure (Maes 2012, not cited); adds link to inflammation, CMI and symptom severity, but no healthy controls

result: In US CFS patients from regions like the 2009 study, low-level XMRV qPCR signals in 15% did not differ from controls, could not be confirmed by product isolation, vanished on PBMC stimulation, and no XMRV gp70 antibody was found; MLV sequences were equally frequent in patients and controls.
reason: Independent cohort, same XMRV PCR/serology tests, negative as the finding states

result: No XMRV gag/env DNA (72 patients), antibodies (62), p30 antigen (50), plasma viremia (9) or infectious virus by co-culture (113) was detected in any Quebec CFS patient.
reason: Independent cohort with multiple assays, all negative for XMRV

result: Phylogenetic analysis of MLV-like sequences from CFS patients sampled 15 years apart strongly rejected within-patient evolution; the two time points carried distinct endogenous murine retroviruses, indicating contamination.
reason: Reanalysis of existing sequences, not a new cohort; adds evidence on the contamination mechanism

result: Among 143,000 adults aged 18-64 in three English primary-care regions, minimum ME/CFS prevalence was 0.2% (0.19% CDC-1994, 0.11% Canadian, 0.03% ECD) with yearly incidence 0.015%.

In monozygotic twins discordant for CFS, no PBMC sample was XMRV-positive by 3 PCR assays; one plasma sample from an unaffected co-twin was RT-PCR positive but same-day serum and follow-up plasma were negative.
reason: Independent cohort, validated XMRV assays, no association; small sample

result: Mitochondrial content was lower in CFS than healthy controls while respiratory chain complex activities corrected for content were normal; ATP production rate and complex I, III and IV activity were higher in CFS than in two mitochondrial-disorder groups.
reason: Abstract does not state blood cells; a diagnostic comparison with mitochondrial disorders using ATP production rate implies muscle tissue, matching the lower muscle mitochondrial capacity finding (tissue inferred, not stated)

result: VBM in 25 CFS vs 25 controls: midbrain white matter volume fell with fatigue duration, CFS-control interactions with hemodynamic scores appeared in brainstem, prefrontal WM, pons and hypothalamus, and brainstem GM volume correlated strongly with pulse pressure.
reason: Brainstem volume/signal differences (Barnden 2011, not cited); same Griffith group so not fully independent

result: Blinded testing of 100 CFS patients, 200 controls and original-study samples found no XMRV/MLV sequences, infectious virus or antibodies; trace mouse DNA in Taq polymerase explained some earlier positives.
reason: Large blinded study including original samples, negative, with a contamination source shown

result: PCR of cerebrospinal fluid from 43 CFS patients found no XMRV or multiple other common viruses.
reason: Independent cohort, XMRV PCR negative, in CSF; no controls
